label.trigger: Untrusted text containing <, >, &, a double quote or an apostrophe is passed to encodeNonAsciiHTML, or to encode() with the ASCII mode at the HTML level, and the result is placed into an HTML page; short strings such as a single tag or an attribute fragment show it most clearly.
label.expected_impact: Every markup character that the per-character scan examines is judged harmless and copied through as is; only those the regex fallback happens to land on after a long clean stretch get turned into entities. Short inputs come back unchanged, so text rendered through this encoder can open elements or leave a quoted attribute, which is a cross-site scripting hole for any page that relies on it.

context_locations.note: The imported mask is laid out for code points 32 to 63, as its trailing remark lists, so in a four-word table it has to sit at index 1.

anchors.start: function isEncodable(bitset: Uint32Array, code: number): boolean {

context_locations.note: Selects the word by code >>> 5, so all five XML specials, which lie between 32 and 63, are looked up in word 1 and read as clear.
The affected public encoder pairs the table with the shared regex; the inline scan trusts the table and the regex only takes over once a window of clean characters is exhausted.
The generic encode() entry routes the ASCII mode at the HTML level to this encoder, so callers of the package's main function are exposed as well.

known_counterevidence.note: encodeXML tests the same mask directly with its own 32-to-63 range check, so XML encoding still escapes markup; findings against encodeXML, escapeUTF8 or the attribute and text escapers do not match.
Markup characters that the shared regex fallback lands on are still encoded, so longer sample inputs come out partly escaped and can make the encoder look correct at a glance.

label.fix_summary: Put XML_BITSET_VALUE into the second slot of the four-word table (index 1, code points 32 to 63) so the per-character test agrees with the shared regex and every XML special character is encoded.

check.summary: Standalone ES module copied into the work copy; it loads src/encode.ts directly through node type stripping and a resolve hook for the relative .js imports, encodes eight short strings with encodeNonAsciiHTML and prints a MISMATCH line for each output that differs from the expected entities.

verification.summary: verify --run-checks with node v24.18.0: on before the script prints seven MISMATCH lines (for example '<b>' comes back unchanged) and exits 1; on after all eight cases agree and it exits 0. The TypeScript sources run unbuilt through node's built-in type stripping with a module.registerHooks resolve hook; nothing is installed. The project's own vitest suite was not run. The html5lib-tests submodule under test/fixtures is not written to the trees and is not used.
